scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, slightly outside the standard 30-day policy window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tyrone Jackson and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Jackson. I understand how frustrating it is to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8829-4410 and the email is t.jackson@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The last four digits are 4492 and my zip code is 90210.

Thank you, Mr. Jackson. I have verified your account. I see the cancellation was processed on day 34 as you mentioned. While our standard 'Service Satisfaction Policy' mandates a 30-day window for full refunds, I can see your account has been in good standing for three years. Given your circumstances, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to our policy.
That would be wonderful, thank you so much for understanding.

It is my pleasure. I have processed the refund for the subscription fee of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: Agent verified the account and applied a one-time exception to the 30-day refund policy due to the customer's long-standing account history, successfully issuing the refund.
